questions.question: In a Central Processing Unit (CPU), what is the primary function of the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)?
options: To fetch instructions from memory
To perform arithmetic operations (e.g., addition, subtraction) and logical operations (e.g., AND, OR)
To store data temporarily in registers
To manage communication with input/output devices
To decode instructions and control other CPU components

questions.question: In digital IC design, what does a 'netlist' primarily represent?
options: A graphical layout of the silicon masks used for fabrication
A textual description of the connectivity between logical components and their instances (gates, flip-flops, etc.)
A specification for the operating voltage and clock frequency of the circuit
A high-level behavioral description of the circuit written in a Hardware Description Language (HDL)
The compiled binary code that a processor executes

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a key difference between an Application-Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) and a Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA)?
options: ASICs are programmable by the user after manufacturing, while FPGAs are not.
FPGAs offer higher performance and lower power consumption for specific tasks compared to ASICs.
ASICs are typically designed for low-volume prototyping, while FPGAs are for mass production.
FPGAs can be reconfigured to implement different logic functions after fabrication, whereas ASICs are fixed.
ASICs do not require a clock signal for operation, while FPGAs rely heavily on it.

questions.question: Which power management technique involves selectively cutting off the power supply to inactive functional blocks within an IC to significantly reduce static (leakage) power consumption?
options: Clock Gating
Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS)
Pipeline Flushing
Power Gating
Architectural Throttling

questions.question: Which architectural concept allows a single CPU core to execute multiple independent threads concurrently by rapidly switching between them, often used to hide memory latency or I/O stalls?
options: Single Instruction, Multiple Data (SIMD)
Out-of-Order Execution
Hardware Multithreading (e.g., SMT/Hyperthreading)
Vector Processing
Distributed Shared Memory
